I've hit my time limit, so I'm giving you the brief now with only what I actually opened and read. Two parts of the request did **not** get completed — I flag them honestly at the end.

---

# Career Brief: Media/Entertainment IT‑Engineer Entry Path (LA)

## 1. What employers expect — recurring requirements
I pulled these from two employer‑side job specs I actually read (a Post‑Production Engineer spec on jobed.ai and a Media Engineer spec on torchora.com), cross‑checked against a live posting. The requirements that kept repeating:

1. **Post‑production software + codec/format fluency** — Avid, Adobe, DaVinci Resolve, Pro Tools; codecs (H.264/265, VP9, AV1), container formats, and understanding editing/mixing/mastering workflows.
2. **Networked storage, backup & media asset management** — Avid/Quantum/Isilon, backup/archiving, and MAM/DAM platforms (Dalet, Avid MediaCentral, EVS).
3. **Core IT infrastructure: networking, OS, troubleshooting** — TCP/IP/multicast, Windows + Linux/Windows Server, server/network topology, hardware/software troubleshooting, and 24/7 support.
4. **Cloud, streaming & scripting (the differentiator)** — AWS/GCP/Azure media services (e.g., AWS Elemental), HLS/MPEG‑DASH/SRT/RTMP, Python/Bash automation, and monitoring (Grafana/Prometheus/Datadog).
5. **Degree + experience baseline** — Bachelor's in media tech / CS / broadcast / electrical / IT; the media‑engineer spec cites 3–7 years, while an entry "associate" role (see job below) accepts 1+ years plus a 2/4‑year technical degree.

**Is it realistically trainable into?** Yes — the recurring requirements are mostly standard IT competencies (networking, OS, storage, troubleshooting) plus a media‑specific layer (codecs, MAM, post software). The media layer is learnable on the job; the IT foundation is the trainable part.

## 2. Concrete training / certification routes (≥2)
From the certification sources I read (CompTIA, AWS, Cisco, plus the media‑engineer spec that names specific certs as "preferred"):
- **CompTIA stack** (A+ → Network+ → Security+): vendor‑neutral IT foundation; the standard entry‑level credential path.
- **AWS certifications** (Cloud Practitioner → Solutions Architect – Associate → SysOps/DevOps): directly relevant because employers want cloud media services (AWS Elemental) experience.
- **Cisco CCNA**: networking validation — explicitly listed as a *preferred* credential in the media‑engineer spec, and Cisco/Harmonic certs are "preferred" in the live WBD posting.

So a realistic route: CompTIA Network+ (or A+ first) → CCNA → AWS Cloud Practitioner/Associate, paired with hands‑on Avid/Resolve and a small storage/MAM project.

## 3. Local 700 (IATSE) — West Coast / LA entry path
From the actual guild page (editorsguild.com/Join/Join‑West‑Coast) — **this is the page I left open for you.** Key facts in the guild's own words:

- **Get a union job first.** The guild encourages you to first secure a union job, then you **must join Local 700 within 30 days of your hire date.**
- **Roster before the job (LA‑specific).** Most classifications working in **Los Angeles County must be on the CSATF "Industry Experience Roster" before accepting union employment** — employers must give hiring preference to people already on the roster.
- **Roster ≠ membership.** Applying for roster placement is a separate process from applying for membership; one does not trigger the other.
- **Qualifying experience.** Work must be "like the work covered by the Local 700 Agreements or Videotape Supplemental Agreement," performed in the US and/or Puerto Rico. Industrial/educational films do **not** count; SVOD varies (verify with a Roster Specialist). ("Engineer" is one of the listed classifications.)
- **Paperwork to submit to CSATF:** a letter from a non‑union employer (on company letterhead) **plus** proof of payment (W‑2s, 1099s, paystubs, or cancelled checks), payment no less than California minimum wage.
- **Fees for the roster:** **No fees** to get on the roster; handled online via **www.thehub.org**.
- **Safety courses required:** A (General Production Safety), HP1, and WVP for all classifications (Sound classifications also need Course K).
- **Orientation:** a New Member Orientation Meeting (via Zoom) covering roster, membership, pension/health, and meeting organizers/field reps.
- **Initiation & processing fee:** a **one‑time** fee (varies by the contract your employer/project is signed to); a **payment plan is half down, half within 6 months** (checks, money orders, credit card).
- **Contacts:** Membership Dept — Tracy Pacio (323) 978‑1087, Tylene Joye (323) 978‑1085, membership@editorsguild.com. CSATF — 2710 Winona Ave, Burbank, CA 91504, (818) 565‑0550, reception@csatf.org.

**Union route vs. training route:** the union path is *experience‑gated* (you need documented qualifying work before you can get on the roster, and a union job before you can join), whereas the broader training path is *credential/skill‑gated*. Realistically, most people build the IT skills + a little qualifying work first, then use the roster to move into a union post job.

## 4. Current job examples (LA / West Coast)
I was able to confirm and open **one** live, publicly accessible LA‑area posting in a separate tab (the tab I left open). I could **not** confirm a second live public LA posting — the closest direct matches were either filled, member‑gated, or Canada‑based (details below).

**Posting 1 — LIVE (open in a tab for you):**
- **Title:** Associate BIT Field Engineer (Associate Broadcast & IT Support)
- **Company:** Warner Bros. Discovery
- **Location:** Burbank, CA (hybrid)
- **Pay (as posted):** $70,004 – $130,008/yr
- **Connection to the requirements:** 24/7 broadcast/production IT support; "proficient IT support and some electronics skills"; server/networking/OS (Windows, Unix); satellite/microwave/streaming transmission; AutoCAD + ITSM ticketing; **preferred certs: Cisco, Harmonic.** This is a strong, near‑entry match (1+ yrs experience, 2/4‑yr technical degree in electronics or computer engineering).
- **Visa / work authorization:** No visa‑sponsorship statement. The EOE language lists "citizenship status" as a protected category (i.e., they don't discriminate on it), but it does **not** say they sponsor. **Also note a hard requirement: a CDL Class B license** and ability to lift 50 lbs.

**Posting 2 — attempted, but not a usable live LA posting:**
- **Disney Entertainment Television — "Post Production Engineer (Audio)," Los Angeles:** a *perfect* skill match (Avid Pro Tools, S6 consoles, Nexis storage, Quantum/Isilon, macOS/Windows/Linux, 4 yrs experience, $55.18/hr, NABET‑CWA union‑covered) — **but it is marked FILLED** (removed 2/1/2024). Useful as a requirements reference, not a live opening.
- **KTLA — "Material Manager," Los Angeles:** live and a media‑asset‑management match, but **member‑login only** on the board (I could not view the public details).
- **Entertainment Partners — "Technical Support Engineer":** a real IT‑support role, but **Ontario, Canada**, not LA.

So, to be straight with you: I only secured **one** confirmed live public LA/West Coast posting in a separate tab (WBD). If you want a true side‑by‑side of two open roles, the best next move is to log in to EntertainmentCareers.Net (for the KTLA and other member listings) or check a company career site directly.

## 5. Rosie O'Donnell / Donald Trump feud timeline
**Not completed.** I ran out of time before doing this final Google research step, so I have no verified dated moments to give you. I'm not going to invent dates. If you want, I can do this as a short follow‑up.

---

## Pages I left open for you to review
- **IATSE Local 700 — "Join West Coast"** (editorsguild.com/Join/Join‑West‑Coast) — the most useful Local 700 page; exact wording on the 30‑day rule, CSATF roster, paperwork, no roster fee, safety courses, and initiation fee/payment plan.
- **Warner Bros. Discovery — Associate BIT Field Engineer** (Burbank) — the one confirmed live LA‑area posting, with full requirements, pay range, and work‑authorization language.

(Honest note: Google returned a captcha early on, so I did all web searching through DuckDuckGo/Bing and then opened the real source pages directly. I also could not complete the second live job posting and the feud timeline — flagged above.)
